subject: physiology
title: Starling Forces, Oedema Pathogenesis, and Homeostasis

steps.tx: Fluid exchange across the microvascular capillary wall is governed by the classic balance of hydrostatic and colloid osmotic pressures, formulated as the **Starling forces**. Net fluid filtration equals the capillary hydraulic filtration coefficient multiplied by the difference between transmembrane hydrostatic pressure gradients and transmembrane oncotic pressure gradients across the endothelial barrier.
steps.say: Capillary fluid exchange is governed by Starling forces: the balance between hydrostatic pressure pushing fluid out and oncotic pressure drawing fluid back in.

vis.alt: Starling capillary filtration and oncotic absorption forces.
vis.caption: Microvascular Starling pressures governing capillary fluid filtration and reabsorption. [Credit: StewardMD]

steps.tx: Four primary pressures determine fluid filtration along the capillary bed. Capillary hydrostatic pressure pushes fluid into the interstitium, opposed by interstitial fluid hydrostatic pressure. Conversely, plasma **colloid osmotic pressure**, generated almost entirely by circulating serum albumin, draws fluid back into the capillary lumen, opposed by the small interstitial fluid oncotic pressure.
steps.say: Four pressures govern filtration: capillary hydrostatic pressure pushes fluid out, while plasma oncotic pressure generated by albumin pulls fluid back inward.

steps.tx: Along a typical somatic capillary, hydrostatic pressure drops from thirty-five millimetres of mercury at the arteriolar end to fifteen millimetres at the venular end, while oncotic pressure remains stable near twenty-eight millimetres. Consequently, filtration dominates at the arteriolar end, but net absorption occurs at the venular end. Overall, a small daily net filtration of two to four litres enters the **lymphatic drainage** system.
steps.say: Filtration occurs at the arteriolar end and reabsorption at the venular end. A small net excess of filtered fluid is returned to circulation by lymphatics.

nodes.label: Arteriolar Capillary End: Pc Exceeds Plasma Oncotic Pressure (Net Filtration)
Venular Capillary End: Oncotic Pressure Exceeds Pc (Net Reabsorption)
Daily Net Filtrate Excess of 2 to 4 Litres Enters Interstitium
Terminal Lymphatic Vessels Return Fluid to Venous Circulation

steps.tx: Abnormal expansion of the interstitial fluid compartment produces clinical **oedema**. Oedema occurs whenever net microvascular filtration outstrips lymphatic drainage capacity. Four fundamental pathophysiological derangements trigger this state: elevated capillary hydrostatic pressure, reduced plasma oncotic pressure, increased microvascular permeability, and mechanical obstruction of lymphatic return.
steps.say: Oedema occurs when microvascular filtration exceeds lymphatic clearance, caused by raised venous pressure, hypoalbuminaemia, leaky capillaries, or lymphatic block.

right.title: Permeability Oedema
points: Accompanied by local erythema, warmth, and pain

steps.tx: In nephrotic syndrome and severe hepatic cirrhosis, plasma albumin concentration drops below twenty-five grams per litre. This marked reduction in **plasma oncotic pressure** diminishes the inward Starling reabsorptive force, shifting the filtration-absorption balance toward continuous fluid loss into tissue spaces and serosal cavities, producing ascites and anasarca.
steps.say: Hypoalbuminaemia in cirrhosis or nephrotic syndrome lowers plasma oncotic pressure, driving continuous fluid filtration into tissue spaces and serous cavities.

nodes.label: Urinary Loss or Impaired Hepatic Synthesis of Albumin
Fall in Plasma Colloid Osmotic Pressure (< 25 g/L)
Unchecked Starling Capillary Filtration into Interstitium
Development of Generalised Pitting Oedema and Ascites

steps.tx: Clinical examination detects interstitial expansion as indentation after digital pressure, designated **pitting oedema**. In dependent subcutaneous tissues such as the pretibial region or sacrum, sustained thumb pressure displaces mobile interstitial free water radially through the collagen matrix. Grading ranges from one-plus for subtle indentation to four-plus for deep, persistent pits that take minutes to refill.
steps.say: Digital pressure over the shin or sacrum displaces interstitial water, demonstrating pitting oedema graded from one-plus to four-plus based on depth and rebound.

vis.alt: Clinical assessment and distribution of pitting oedema.
vis.caption: Clinical examination and pitting grading of dependent subcutaneous oedema. [Credit: StewardMD]

steps.tx: Stability of the internal fluid environment is maintained by physiological control systems operating via **negative feedback**. In a negative feedback loop, any deviation of a controlled variable such as arterial pressure or plasma osmolarity triggers sensor activation that elicits counteracting effector responses, returning the regulated parameter toward its predetermined homeostatic set point.
steps.say: Homeostasis is maintained by negative feedback loops, where any deviation of a regulated variable triggers corrective responses that restore the set point.

nodes.label: Controlled Variable Deviates from Set Point (e.g., Blood Pressure Falls)
Physiological Receptors Detect Error (Carotid Sinus Baroreceptors)
Target Parameter Returns Toward Normal Set Point

steps.tx: In contrast, **positive feedback** loops amplify an initial perturbation, driving physiological systems toward a rapid, all-or-none conclusion. While uncontrolled positive feedback leads to vicious pathophysiological spirals like haemorrhagic shock, controlled positive feedback orchestrates essential physiological events including the voltage-gated sodium influx of an action potential, the Ferguson oxytocin delivery reflex, and the platelet activation cascade.
steps.say: Positive feedback amplifies initial deviations toward an explosive climax. While dangerous in shock, it drives vital processes like action potentials and labor.

left.title: Negative Feedback
points: Corrects perturbations back to set point
Operates continuously for arterial pressure and pH

right.title: Positive Feedback
points: Drives variable further away from initial state
Terminates by an external climax or limit
Examples: Action potential upstroke, parturition, clotting
